hardinessNote: Hardy through a cold UK winter, approximately −15 to −10°C (RHS 351299).
visual: Scented spring flowers in mixed yellow, orange, red and purple · compact, bushy bedding plant
soilWarning: Avoid ground with club root history
water: Water in after planting and in dry spring spells; once rooted it needs little extra.
prune: Deadhead to prolong flowering. Usually lifted after flowering as spring bedding.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten: all parts, especially the seeds, contain heart-affecting compounds that can cause sickness. Keep children, dogs and cats from chewing it.
cvs: 'Fire King' – taller, orange-red · 'Blood Red' – deep red, taller · 'Persian Carpet' – mixed pastel shades
resilience: Tough through winter cold and wind once planted. Short-lived, best treated as spring bedding. Pests: aphids, flea beetle, club root, downy mildew.
uses: Spring bedding · containers · window boxes · cottage borders · pairs with tulips
foliage: evergreen; narrow lance-shaped mid to dark green leaves
pollination: not applicable; grown for flowers, not fruit
uncertain: hardiness: Erysimum cheiri is hardy across most of the UK, but the RHS band for this seed series was not checked. H4 was chosen conservatively and may be H5.
height and spread: the series is sold as compact (about 25–30 cm). The figures were not confirmed against breeder data and no label was supplied.
peak: classic wallflowers flower Mar-May. Some modern series are marketed as also flowering in autumn or winter, which was not confirmed for Sugar Rush.
hue: this is a colour mix, so 30 (orange) is a representative midpoint, not a single dominant colour.
compliance: whether Sugar Rush has plant breeders' rights or a registered series code is unknown, so the field is left blank.
clay: wallflowers prefer sharp drainage and dislike wet heavy soil, but tolerance of improved clay is not established, so the field is left blank.
stockForm: assumed container (pots or packs). Traditional wallflowers are also sold bare-root in autumn, which was not confirmed for this series.
cvs: the colour names of the separate Sugar Rush selections were not confident, so classic E. cheiri cultivars are listed instead.
toxicity: Erysimum contains cardiac glycosides. Severity in practice is believed to be low to moderate. The wording was chosen to give the Toxic tier without overstating it.
sunMin: 50 is a judgement that it tolerates part shade with fewer flowers.
ratings: pestRisk, thirst, careLevel and growthSpeed are judged from general wallflower behaviour.

hardinessNote: Very hardy throughout the UK, tolerating winters colder than -20°C.
visual: Bright golden-yellow lobed leaves, flushed copper in spring · domed clusters of small white to pinkish flowers in early summer · peeling bark in winter
water: Water regularly in the first summer; afterwards only in prolonged dry spells.
prune: After flowering, remove a few of the oldest stems at the base. A hard cut in late winter gives the brightest new foliage but fewer flowers.
cvs: 'Dart's Gold' – older golden form · DIABOLO ('Monlo') – dark purple leaves · 'Lady in Red' – red-purple leaves · 'Little Devil' – dwarf, purple
resilience: Very cold-hardy and tolerant of clay and wind once established. Pests: powdery mildew in dry summers, occasional aphids.
uses: Mixed borders · foliage contrast with purple shrubs · informal hedging · cut stems
uncertain: height: the cultivar's mature height is not known with confidence and no label was supplied. The species is about 2-3 m, but this selection may be more compact.
spread: the cultivar's mature spread is not known with confidence and no label was supplied. Left blank, although the card needs a spread to draw the rails.
hardiness: H7 is based on the RHS rating for the species and other golden cultivars such as 'Dart's Gold'. It has not been confirmed for 'Minange' specifically.
peak: given as the golden-foliage season. Flowering is roughly Jun, and the exact months for this cultivar are unchecked.
hue: 52 assumes the dominant feature is gold-yellow foliage. Spring leaves may be more orange-gold and fade to lime later in the season.
sunMin: left null. Golden foliage greens in shade, and the lowest acceptable light is not established.
sunNeed: a judgement. The cultivar's tendency to scorch in hot full sun is not confirmed.
soil/soilWarning: based on species preferences (moist but well-drained, acid to neutral; chlorosis on shallow chalk), not cultivar data.
toxicity: no hazard is recorded for Physocarpus as far as known. This should be checked online.
compliance: the PBR grant number is unknown. The breeder is believed to be Minier (France) but this is unconfirmed.
ratings (pestRisk, thirst, careLevel, growthSpeed): judged from the species.

hardinessNote: Hardy through most of the UK in an average winter, approximately -10 to -5°C; top growth may be cut back by hard frost but usually regrows from the base.
visual: Domed heads of fragrant deep rose-pink flowers in late summer · large heart-shaped dark leaves on upright suckering stems
soilWarning: Suckers spread widely; site with care
water: Water regularly in the first summer; established plants need watering only in prolonged dry spells.
prune: Cut frost-damaged or old stems to the base in spring. Remove unwanted suckers to keep it in bounds.
toxicity: No record for this species; some Clerodendrum can cause mild stomach upset if eaten and skin irritation, so wear gloves if sensitive.
cvs: 'Pink Diamond' – cream-edged variegated leaves, less vigorous
resilience: Recovers well from hard winters by regrowing from the base; spreads vigorously by suckers. Leaves smell unpleasant when crushed. Pests: generally trouble-free.
uses: Late-summer borders · shrub borders · wildlife and pollinator planting · sheltered gardens
foliage: deciduous; large heart-shaped dark green leaves, unpleasant-smelling when crushed
uncertain: hardiness: H4 as remembered from the RHS profile, not checked online
height and spread: 1.5–2.5 m as remembered; spread can increase considerably through suckering, so verify
peak: Aug-Sep as remembered; flowering may continue into October in mild years
toxicity: no hazard listing recalled for C. bungei, but this is not confirmed and should be checked before printing
sunMin: part-shade tolerance (50) is a judgement, not a sourced figure
clay: left blank because tolerance of heavy clay is not established
container: 'with care' is a judgement based on its suckering habit
cvs: 'Pink Diamond' is the only sibling cultivar remembered with confidence

hardiness, height, spread: RHS 29541 agrees (H4, 1.5–2.5 × 1.5–2.5 m); spreads further by suckers.

peak: Aug-Sep kept; RHS gives late summer and autumn, no months.
